intervention_and_type: 4-phenylbutyrate and bile-acid chemical chaperones, taken together as a class (drug class; formulation UNKNOWN)
research_objective: broad_durable_recovery (restoring the function of residual protein)
genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track B: lesion-specific, a Q230P-class missense with residual protein; no meaning for null, nonsense or splice lesions
depth_of_benefit_sought: deep: function per molecule of the rescued protein; a larger amount of protein is not function and is not read as rescue
biological_effect_sought: Raise the soluble, native, functional pool of a destabilised WWOX missense protein (folding or trafficking fate).
PRIORITY_position_and_work_order_reason: F3 (favourable hypothesis from the target; intervention not tested in WWOX). Work order: resolve a premise - is the Q230P-class protein made then cleared, by which route, and does returned protein carry function per molecule.
MODEL_position_P3_P2: None. Not in the P3 universe (card-linked families were firewalled out of every method) and P3 tested a transcript module, not protein fate. P2: a class with a catalogued target row only for HDAC at enzyme level; no chaperone target row in ChEMBL, GtoPdb or DGIdb.
OBSERVED_wwox_specific_evidence: None for the intervention in any WWOX system. The lesion side: one patient-fibroblast blot (one membrane, one exposure) shows transcript comparable to reference lines and no detectable protein band; fractions not separated.
premise_demonstrated: Other proteins: chemical chaperone or osmolyte raised a destabilised mutant with protein and function read together in some cases (GAT-1 variant; a soluble cytosolic client roughly doubled in soluble fraction). All are outside WWOX.
premise_missing: Where the Q230P-class protein is lost (never made, cleared, insoluble, epitope-invisible); any per-molecule WWOX function assay; whether the lesion is a stability lesion; which of three mechanism classes (chaperoning, HDAC6/HSP90 acetylation, class-I HDAC transcription) operates.
external_precedents_with_reading_depth: Several cell, worm, fly, zebrafish and short mouse precedents in other proteins: cards record complete or partial full-text reads for the R1 papers; no WWOX test. Rationale was withdrawn once in this repository and narrowed, not refuted (IT5 P8).
potentially_opposed_effects: Wild-type protein rises too (not mutant-specific); partly trafficked variant not rescued by the class in one precedent; butyrate raised immature total protein with small function gain; toxicity ceiling near 4 mM in one paper; HDAC inhibition is quantitatively available at the applied levels and could be the operating mechanism, with transcriptional side effects.
potency_with_assay_context: No numeric value for any chaperone mechanism (no folding, binding or thermal-shift datum in ChEMBL, GtoPdb or DGIdb). Only HDAC inhibition is quantified: Ki about 6.3 uM for phenylbutyrate on HDAC in human HeLa nuclear extract (fluorimetric assay, ChEMBL), recombinant enzymes tens to hundreds of uM; cell experiments applied about 0.5 to 10 mM for a day (about 8 to 78 times the HDAC IC50; arithmetic, not occupancy); bile acid 100 uM in cells.
human_exposure: Phenylbutyrate sodium has a ChEMBL mechanism of ammonia scavenging; the label was not searched here (label_lookup NOT_ATTEMPTED). Paediatric suitability for this purpose UNKNOWN.
brain_penetration: UNKNOWN: brain exposure beside mutant-protein level was not measured in any precedent read; mouse exposures were days.
next_decision_changing_experiment: Build the wild-type function ruler first: isogenic WWOX-null human neural line, wild-type WWOX titrated over at least five levels with a Tier 1 WW1-dependent readout and measured protein; then place the Q230P-class allele on the curve; only then a lever panel (class-I HDAC inhibitor; HDAC6-selective or pan-HDAC; HDAC-free chaperone and osmolytes) with mRNA flat and the null line unaffected as conditions. Outcomes fixed in advance in the card.

intervention_and_type: Proteasome-inhibitor class (research or oncology agents), class level only; no agent named (drug class)
genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track B: Q230P-class missense that is a proteasome substrate; a lysosomal route would make it ineffective; no meaning for null lesions
depth_of_benefit_sought: deep only if stabilisation suffices; stabilisation without refolding is expected to raise inactive or insoluble protein for catalytic or folding lesions
biological_effect_sought: Block degradation of a destabilised missense protein so that more reaches a functional state.
PRIORITY_position_and_work_order_reason: F3 (from the target; not tested in WWOX). Same work-order entry as CMP-01: the route and function question must be answered before either lever.
MODEL_position_P3_P2: None; outside the P3 universe and not a transcript question.
OBSERVED_wwox_specific_evidence: None for the intervention. No fractionation, half-life, inhibitor or synthesis datum exists for the exact variant.
premise_demonstrated: Cytosolic enzyme precedent (CBS): proteasome inhibition restored activity in vivo for a regulatory-domain allele and partly for catalytic-domain alleles; the route can be resolved per allele. Not WWOX.
premise_missing: That the Q230P-class protein is made and then cleared by the proteasome (the repository red-team record expects a lysosomal route); that recovered protein is functional; a safe exposure window.
external_precedents_with_reading_depth: CBS and ASPA precedents read at the passages the card cites (IT6 P6, 17 statements checked): boost without repair, insoluble stabilised protein (ASPA), protein up with activity flat (CBS with HSP70 or HSF1 co-expression), toxic windows including in controls.
potentially_opposed_effects: Gain applies to wild type too (CBS wild-type half-life up about 7.7-fold); immune toxicity and toxic windows in controls; a heat-shock response confounds the readout; allele-selective failure (one allele not rescued in the mouse).
potency_with_assay_context: UNKNOWN for WWOX; the closest precedent is toxicity-bounded and its values are not reproduced in the card.
human_exposure: UNKNOWN for this purpose; oncology agents exist but no agent is proposed here.
next_decision_changing_experiment: Route-first fate experiment on the exact variant in an expression-matched WWOX-null human system: soluble, pellet and total protein, mRNA in the same wells, pulse-chase half-life, proteasome, lysosome and ERAD arms side by side each on the ruler line and the null line with a viability readout. No protein with synthesis present closes this card for the allele.

intervention_and_type: AAV9 carrying human WWOX cDNA under a neuronal promoter (gene addition; not a small molecule)
genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track A: allele-blind in design (replaces the missing gene product); tested only in a null mouse; response in a missense or compound context with residual function is unmeasured
depth_of_benefit_sought: deep: multi-endpoint restoration; shown for prevention in an early window, not for recovery after onset (one organoid endpoint aside)
biological_effect_sought: Restore WWOX dosage in neurons so that seizure-like discharges, survival, growth and myelination approach wild type.
PRIORITY_position_and_work_order_reason: C01 F2 on gene addition (one experiment, n 5, flagged); C04 F1 on gene addition (GFAP-positive cell count, high dose, controlled) and C2 on glycaemia and growth (glucose null beside body-weight benefit). Work order: verify a hypothesis - threshold or gradient, and prevented versus recovered after onset.
MODEL_position_P3_P2: None. Gene addition is not a compound question; P2 counts it as direction-evaluable by target only (zero signed records on the need target) and P3 did not touch it.
OBSERVED_wwox_specific_evidence: Wwox-null mouse, vector given P0 to P5: spike-wave discharges not distinguishable from wild type at the high level (blinded, n 5); survival to 300 days at the high level comparable to the wild-type arm, the low level postpones death; weight equal at one age but survivor-conditioned; glucose unchanged; myelination dose relation never quantified; gliosis binary against wild type. Organoid AAV9-WWOX at week 10: hyperexcitability and transcript-level changes read at week 16 against non-treated organoids (not vector-treated).
premise_demonstrated: Prevention of the null phenotype by neuronal WWOX in the earliest postnatal window, in the strongest causal design of the corpus; neuron-restricted deletion reproduces the phenotype and neuron-restricted replacement reverses it.
premise_missing: Treatment after onset (mouse: unmeasured after P5); threshold versus steep continuum (two dose points); independent replication (two papers share a senior author); transfer to missense or compound alleles; tumour surveillance for an irreversibly delivered pro-apoptotic tumour suppressor; absolute vector quantity (uncertain by a factor of two in the source).
external_precedents_with_reading_depth: The two mouse papers and the organoid paper are the only sources; the survival and motor comparators were re-read at the source in IT6 P2; the organoid single-cell data are deposited but not accessible. No other gene-addition precedent is used.
potentially_opposed_effects: Over-expression of a pro-apoptotic tumour suppressor with no ceiling measured and no surveillance; regionally uneven biodistribution; glucose endpoints null beside weight benefit (C2 on that need); wild-type arm itself lost about 29 percent by 300 days.
potency_with_assay_context: Not applicable in the small-molecule sense; vector quantity convention undeclared by the source; no figure reproduced.
human_exposure: No human use in the corpus; the human product, construct and titre are UNKNOWN.
brain_penetration: Mouse: delivery to brain shown by expression, regionally uneven; human route and penetration UNKNOWN.
next_decision_changing_experiment: An intermediate-level arm (a fraction of the high level) carried to 300 days with survival, weight, glucose, ECoG and quantified myelin in the same animals, plus a pre-treatment baseline and treated-after-onset arms with a same-age untreated comparator. A failure moves the card to C2 by rule; a treated-after-onset arm decides whether the word recovery may be used.
experiment_status: PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work; needs a laboratory holding the vector, none known here

intervention_and_type: LDH-directed levers: stiripentol (approved paediatric antiseizure drug, weak LDH inhibition in vitro), research LDHA inhibitors, an LDHA-directed oligonucleotide (liver-directed) (drug class)
genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track A: allele-blind downstream metabolic lever; whether the axis is preserved in a catalytic-domain missense allele is an inference only
depth_of_benefit_sought: partial: a metabolic consequence, not restoration of WWOX; no endpoint benefit is claimed
biological_effect_sought: Lower LDH activity or lactate production where a raised glycolytic and lactate state is deleterious.
PRIORITY_position_and_work_order_reason: F3 on lactate/LDH (target-engagement and tool-compound assays and a fly genetic precedent only; candidate showed poor engagement; counter tags counted); P3 on mitochondrial respiration. Work order: verify a hypothesis - is LDH activity or lactate raised in WWOX-deficient neural cells, and does the candidate reach an inhibitory level at all.
MODEL_position_P3_P2: P3 (IT7, exploratory, minimum detectable effect about rho 0.15, independently verified): NO ADDED VALUE of a signed external network (rho 0.047) or a WWOX-enriched network (difference -0.0015) for ranking compounds by opposition of the six-gene module; the signature route is effect not detected, not excluded (rho 0.143, 0.007 under the 0.15 threshold, 90 percent interval 0.039 to 0.243, minimum detectable effect about 0.157), with weak positive counter-evidence to no added value for that route (interval lower bound 0.039, top-decile hit rate 15 percent); module transfer to the P47T deposit INCONCLUSIVE (hippocampus D +0.329, null 95th percentile 0.389 and exact one-sided p 0.060 on the producer's draw, 0.396 and 0.0595 on the verifier's, 5 of 6 genes in the build direction, LDHA +0.48, LDHB -0.10 against). Stiripentol was firewalled out of the P3 universe (card-linked). P2: stiripentol has no signed action on a stable target, so it is not usable by the network method, and has no neural signature in LINCS. No model position for this compound.
OBSERVED_wwox_specific_evidence: Transcript level only: LDHA higher in the knockout organoid and in shRNA progenitors (one library per arm); lactate and LDH activity higher in a human knockout fibroblast line; fly Ldh RNAi improved climbing once in an amyloid plus Wwox-reduction genotype (no Ldh-alone arm, no lactate readout). Human lactate in WWOX deficiency reported normal or extremely low in other sources. No compound has been given to any WWOX-deficient system on this need.
premise_demonstrated: LDHA transcript raised in two human neural transcript systems; HK and LDH activity raised in one human fibroblast line.
premise_missing: LDH activity or lactate in WWOX-deficient human neural cells at matched maturity; that the elevation is not maturity or integrated-stress-response driven; that the candidate engages LDH in brain.
external_precedents_with_reading_depth: Rico-Molina 2024 read in part (inhibition data), Bacq 2024 review opened at the pharmacokinetic passage; Sada 2015 not lawfully acquirable (abstract and secondary descriptions only). Nedosiran shows LDHA lowering tolerated in liver.
potentially_opposed_effects: Stiripentol also inhibits mitochondrial complex I (isolated mouse heart and liver mitochondria, from tens of uM), so a metabolic effect is not an LDH effect and may recruit the integrated stress response; Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models (authors' own citation); LDHB is the discordant gene in the P3 transfer test.
potency_with_assay_context: Stiripentol: 9.9 percent inhibition of recombinant human LDHA at 500 uM, IC50 greater than 500 uM (single-concentration cell-free assay; racemate and enantiomers differ; no fitted potency); a review puts LDH-effective concentrations at 42 to 500 uM, above total plasma levels at effective doses. GSK2837808A potent on LDHA in vitro; no CNS datum retrieved.
human_exposure: Stiripentol: marketed with a paediatric label for Dravet syndrome together with clobazam; free brain concentration estimated 0.2 to 1 uM in a review (secondary). Research LDHA inhibitors: none.
brain_penetration: Stiripentol brain LDH engagement asserted by secondary sources, not verified; catalogue and cached ChEMBL fields give no brain, CSF or blood-brain-barrier statement (P2). Research inhibitors: no datum.
next_decision_changing_experiment: Lactate (isotope or enantiomer resolved) and LDH activity, LDHA and LDHB separately, in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity, with phospho-eIF2 alpha and ATF4 read beside LDH; the fly Ldh-alone arm; only then stiripentol against a selective LDHA tool at matched exposure. If lactate is not raised the need loses its WWOX observation and the card moves to P3 by rule.
experiment_status: PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work

intervention_and_type: Dichloroacetate, the prototype pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase inhibitor (investigational drug)
genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track A: allele-blind in design; WWOX binds HIF1A through WW1, so the axis may be partly preserved in an SDR missense allele (inference)
depth_of_benefit_sought: partial: a metabolic and possibly symptomatic effect; the card pursues no benefit endpoint and sharpens a decision
biological_effect_sought: Release a PDH restraint (lower inhibitory phosphorylation of PDH) so that glucose oxidation rises and lactate falls, if a WWOX-dependent restraint exists.
need_link: NEED-PDH-PYRUVATE-AXIS (also NEED-LACTATE-LDH, NEED-SEIZURE-CONTROL-SYMPTOMATIC, NEED-SYSTEMIC-GLYCAEMIA-GROWTH as endpoint and confounder)
PRIORITY_position_and_work_order_reason: I01: C3 on PDH axis and on seizure control (harm or null outside WWOX with no favourable signal there), F3 on lactate/LDH; E03: F3 on the PDH axis. Work order: verify a hypothesis - is PDH phosphorylation higher in WWOX-deficient neural cells and does a PDK inhibitor change it in a genotype-dependent way without lowering glucose in a hypoglycaemic model.
MODEL_position_P3_P2: P3 (IT7, exploratory, independently verified): the same result as CMP-04 - network routes NO ADDED VALUE, signature route not detected and not excluded (weak positive counter-evidence: lower bound 0.039, top-decile hit rate 15 percent); module transfer inconclusive (null 95th percentile 0.389 and p 0.060 on the producer's draw, 0.396 and 0.0595 on the verifier's); PDK1 is the one down gene (P47T hippocampus -0.08, lower in sign only). DCA is card-linked and firewalled out of P3. P2: DCA is usable by the network method (PDK1 to PDK4, inhibitor, down) and has no LINCS signature, so no signature method applies. No model position for this compound.
OBSERVED_wwox_specific_evidence: PDK1 transcript up and HIF1alpha up in Wwox-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts; PDK transcript higher in a human knockout fibroblast line; PDK1 lower in sign only (inside the single-gene null) in two human neural transcript systems; PDH activity not different in the one human line; no PDH phosphorylation, flux or lactate measurement in any WWOX-deficient neural system. No compound given to any WWOX-deficient system.
premise_demonstrated: The glycolytic end of the chain (LDHA, a HIF-type gene set) is raised in two human neural transcript systems; PDK-PDH restraint is documented after chemoconvulsant seizures in two non-WWOX epilepsy models.
premise_missing: That PDH is restrained in a WWOX-deficient neural system and that the restraint is WWOX-dependent rather than seizure-secondary; the direction of the glucose response in a hypoglycaemic young animal.
external_precedents_with_reading_depth: Paediatric congenital lactic acidosis randomized trial (lactate moved, no clinical outcome in six months), a long-term follow-up, a MELAS trial stopped early for neuropathy; the one seizure-endpoint test in a PDH-restrained model was negative (abstract level, closed); several of these at abstract or review level only.
potentially_opposed_effects: Lowers glucose in adults and gluconeogenic precursors while hypoglycaemia is the Wwox-null phenotype (sign in a hypoglycaemic pup unmeasured); peripheral neuropathy is dose-limiting in adults; urinary oxalate +22 percent in a long-term cohort; rodent hepatotoxicity and neoplasia at high chronic doses; the general mechanism is self-inhibition of its own metabolism (GSTZ1), so exposure rises with repeated administration and varies with haplotype and age, whereas the one paediatric kinetic cohort (17 children) plateaued rather than accumulating - the two statements come from different sources and are not reconciled here; a slight pro-convulsant signal in one test.
potency_with_assay_context: ChEMBL curated mechanism: inhibitor of PDK1 to PDK4 (enzyme level). ChEMBL activity rows for the sodium salt (re-queried on 2026-10-29 after an earlier transient HTTP 500; 39 rows retrieved): enzymatic PDK assays give censored IC50 above 1,000,000 nM (rat PDHK, human PDK and porcine PDHK preparations, primary enzymatic assays), a kinase-Glo assay on PDK1 with PDH E1 as substrate (30 min, origin unknown) EC50 5,700,000 nM, and binding to recombinant human PDK1 by isothermal titration calorimetry Kd above 1,000,000 nM; a cell assay in human skin fibroblasts (increased lactate oxidation) gives EC50 130,000 nM. The gap between cell and enzyme values (about an order of magnitude, enzyme values censored) means no enzyme potency is established and the cellular value is not a target-engagement measure; other rows are cancer-line viability assays and are not PDK potencies.
human_exposure: Investigational, orphan designation for congenital lactic acidosis; paediatric safety record in that disease (follow-up of 110 patient-years); no marketed label in openFDA; availability as a dietary ingredient not established. Drug kinetics in 17 children plateaued rather than accumulating (one cohort; see the opposed-effects cell for the contrast with self-inhibition).
brain_penetration: UNKNOWN: CSF lactate fell in a long-term cohort but drug concentration in the CNS was not measured.
next_decision_changing_experiment: In WWOX-deficient human neural cells against matched controls: PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation with total PDH, PDH activity and a glucose tracer into acetyl-CoA, citrate and lactate, then with a PDK inhibitor against vehicle reading the genotype-by-inhibitor interaction (free DCA exposure and a second inhibitor of different chemistry as controls). Animal arms (glucose, lactate, ketones in P10 to P14 pups) only if the cell result shows restraint. A positive interaction moves the lever from parked to testable; none closes the PDK strand at the premise.
experiment_status: PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work; cell access depends on a deposit that needs an access request that exists as a draft only and is not filed

genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track A: allele-blind in design; mechanism for WWOX UNKNOWN
depth_of_benefit_sought: partial: empirical seizure control; any bypass of a bioenergetic defect is hypothetical

intervention_and_type: NMDAR and AMPAR intervention classes: competitive block (d-APV tool, selfotel), use-dependent pore blockers (memantine, ketamine), GluN2B negative modulators (radiprodil clinical stage), AMPAR antagonists (perampanel approved) (drug classes; a compound named is an identity, not a recommendation)
genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track A: acts on a network state whatever the allele; the one electrophysiology source is a neuron-specific knockout, so missense lesions are untested
depth_of_benefit_sought: partial: reduction of a network state (bursting); the card says no developmental benefit is implied
biological_effect_sought: Lower excitatory gain or bursting in the cortex where d-APV abolishes it; decide whether partial block suffices (lever) or near-complete block is needed (symptom tool).
PRIORITY_position_and_work_order_reason: F3 for F04 (from the target; one WWOX row, d-APV, is a tool compound carried by F01 as F2). Work order: verify a hypothesis - which of three readings (NMDAR gain, permissive necessity, AMPAR-led drive) explains the d-APV-sensitive bursting; the isolated NMDAR current comes first.
MODEL_position_P3_P2: None from P3 (a receptor-physiology question, not a transcript module; memantine and perampanel are card-linked and firewalled). P2: memantine and perampanel are usable by the network method (signed antagonist actions on GRIN and GRIA targets) and have no neural LINCS signature, so the signature method does not apply; the need has 179 linked records by target association only. No model position.
OBSERVED_wwox_specific_evidence: Neuron-specific knockout cortical slice (single paper): d-APV abolishes bursting (5 slices from 3 animals, no significance marker in the figure) and the delayed evoked response; sEPSC about 6 percent higher; sIPSC amplitude 27.5 against 57.3 pA (the larger change is inhibitory); hippocampal slices do not burst. No memantine, ketamine, GluN2B modulator or AMPAR antagonist was applied in a WWOX system.
premise_demonstrated: Bursting needs NMDAR activity in this slice; the knockout rests more depolarised than wild type.
premise_missing: NMDAR gain (versus permissive dependence on depolarisation and weak inhibition); the fraction of NMDAR current that must be blocked; the recording-bath Mg2+; any subunit data; that the finding extends beyond cortex slice or to other alleles.
external_precedents_with_reading_depth: GluN2B negative modulators effective at more than 80 percent of the 27 tested gain-of-function GRIN variants in vitro (abstract only; source form); memantine improvement in any domain in a GRIN series 14 of 19 gain-of-function against 3 of 15 other (partial read; seizure-frequency difference not significant); selfotel stopped in adult stroke and head injury trials. All in gain-of-function disease, where the sign is known.
potentially_opposed_effects: Selfotel failed with a harm signal in adults; NMDAR blockade in the developing rat brain triggers apoptosis (abstract level); memantine accelerated seizure stages in an adult rat oxygen model; perampanel carries a boxed warning for psychiatric and behavioural reactions; sustained NMDAR dampening may affect activity-dependent myelination (F02) in a developing brain; AMPAR block can abolish bursts without discriminating the NMDAR sign.
potency_with_assay_context: Heterogeneous and not a drug property. d-APV: competitive glutamate-site block, full at saturation (rat clones, oocytes). Memantine: IC50 840 nM (GluN1/2A, -60 mV) and 28,070 nM at -40 mV in one closed document (HEK293, human clones, 33-fold shift implausible, flagged UNVERIFIED); FLIPR calcium flux in CHO 3.2 to 31.6 uM; rat oocyte -75 mV 2.7 to 5.6 uM; physiological 1.3 mM Mg2+ lowers memantine block of GluN2A/2B about 20-fold at rest (abstract). Radiprodil: IC50 4 to 70 nM at human-labelled GluN2B (Ca flux, [3H] displacement; assay organism blank). Perampanel: IC50 243 to 6,510 nM (GluA1 or GluA3, CHO-S or HEK293, mixing auxiliary-subunit and isoform conditions, cyclothiazide present). Single-subunit ChEMBL targets return zero rows for pore blockers: pore blockers are curated against complexes (an empty answer is not absence).
human_exposure: Memantine and ketamine approved in adults; memantine label: paediatric safety and effectiveness not established, two controlled studies of 578 children with autism spectrum disorder failed. Perampanel approved from 4 years of age for partial-onset seizures. Radiprodil: 460 adults, 3 infants; paediatric trials selected by gain-of-function variant; no efficacy result found.
brain_penetration: UNKNOWN in the catalogue and cached ChEMBL fields for memantine and perampanel (no brain, CSF or blood-brain-barrier statement); the receptor-state and Mg2+ dependence of block in cortex is the larger uncertainty.
next_decision_changing_experiment: Step E1 in the source preparation (neuron-specific knockout, littermates, P13 to P17, layer II/III): isolated NMDAR current under voltage control with AMPAR and GABA-A blocked, amplitude, decay, NMDA:AMPA ratio, GluN2B and GluN2A shares, resting potential; then d-APV and a GluN2B tool concentration-response on the isolated current, the delayed response and bursts; a pore blocker only afterwards as a translation probe with Mg2+ and holding potential stated. The two reported baseline burst rates must be reconciled first.
experiment_status: PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work; the knockout line is not held here

intervention_and_type: Magnesium as the extracellular divalent cation (supplement or nutrient; preparation unsettled; not a diet)
genotype_lesion_applicability_track: Track A: allele-blind; Track B unmeasured
depth_of_benefit_sought: partial at best: a reduction of a network state; no developmental benefit implied
biological_effect_sought: Restore voltage-dependent NMDAR pore block that a more depolarised resting potential and weaker inhibition relieve.
PRIORITY_position_and_work_order_reason: P3 (the card links the need by mechanism only: no Mg2+ row in a WWOX system and ChEMBL curates the mechanism of the sulfate as unknown, so GRIN target queries never surface it). Work order: same entry as CMP-07, with a graded bath-Mg2+ titration and d-APV as ceiling.
MODEL_position_P3_P2: None. An ion has no signed target row for the network method and no neural LINCS perturbation; the P3 negative does not apply.
OBSERVED_wwox_specific_evidence: None for magnesium: no WWOX measurement of Mg2+, NMDAR current or block was found (zero hits for WWOX with magnesium in the searches run). The convergent WWOX observations are the d-APV result, a resting potential of -73.62 mV in knockout against -79.25 mV in wild type, and halved inhibitory current amplitude.
premise_demonstrated: The knockout slice bursts in a medium whose incubation solution contains 1.3 mM Mg2+ (so the bursting is probably not a magnesium-free artefact; the recording bath is not stated, which is an inference).
premise_missing: That the burst depends on the Mg2+ block; that a reachable Mg2+ rise lowers bursts without altering wild-type activity; that any preparation raises brain extracellular free Mg2+ in a child; serum and CSF Mg in WWOX-DEE.
external_precedents_with_reading_depth: Infantile spasms: intravenous magnesium sulfate with ACTH outperformed ACTH alone in 38 infants (abstract only); an open-label trial with an oral phase (48 analysed, both arms on ACTH and antiseizure drugs) found no difference (p 0.69). One mouse study read: oral magnesium sulfate raised serum Mg and left CSF Mg unchanged; the threonate raised CSF Mg by about a third in healthy mice (six per subgroup).
potentially_opposed_effects: Sustained NMDAR dampening may affect activity-dependent myelination or synaptic maturation in a developing brain (unmeasured); a graded rise in an ion that is already present removes only part of the residual conductance while d-APV removes all; one case on vitamin B6 and zonisamide without relief is recorded as counter-data for a related nutrient strand.
potency_with_assay_context: Arithmetic on borrowed numbers, not a measurement: external Mg2+ IC50 of the NMDA-evoked current 20.9, 53.3 and 173 uM at -90, -70 and -50 mV (P7 rat substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons, whole cell; a different cell type); with the source's resting potentials the unblocked fraction at 1.3 mM Mg2+ is 3.35 percent in knockout against 2.59 percent in wild type (ratio 1.29), and a 15 or 30 percent Mg2+ rise lowers the knockout fraction to 0.87 or 0.78 of its value; a full competitive block gives 0. Single-site occupancy and log-linear voltage dependence are assumed (UNVERIFIED for cortex).
human_exposure: US supplement labels exist for magnesium and its salts by name (DSLD name probe 2026-10-29, not a frequency); the threonate has an authorised EU Novel Food entry whose conditions were not read; Italian register not checked (bot challenge, not bypassed). Access is not efficacy or safety.
brain_penetration: Preparation-dependent and regulated: oral sulfate no CSF change in mouse, threonate about +30 percent; human data not found.
next_decision_changing_experiment: Graded bath Mg2+ around the slice value, in both directions, in knockout, heterozygote and wild-type neocortical slices at P13 to P17 in the source medium, then d-APV as ceiling; endpoints burst incidence, frequency, duration and amplitude, plus NMDA:AMPA ratio; in parallel total and ionised Mg in serum and CSF of knockout against control mice and the CSF response to one oral preparation. A rise that cannot lower bursts inside a reachable range closes the strand.
